stop_classification.description:
Per-aircraft (not per-operation) stop rate: of the distinct tails
seen, how many landed at least once. `all` counts every tail in
the window; `pattern` counts only tails that worked the pattern
(circle/touch-and-go/low-approach/landing), excluding pure
overflights.

code.description: Stable machine-readable code. Branch on this.

message.description: Human-readable detail. Wording may change; do not parse.

airports.description: ICAO codes this key is restricted to, or null for unrestricted.

constants.description:
Values a consumer needs in order to interpret other responses.
Published once here rather than repeated on every row.

pattern_corridor_nm.description:
Perpendicular distance from the published pattern beyond which an
aircraft counts as "off pattern". `fraction_off_pattern` on
/v1/operations is measured against this.

name.description: The label the administrator gave this key.

aircraft_type.description: Airframe model from the registry, when known.

last_reported_at_ts.description: Unix seconds of the most recent public report against this aircraft, or null if it has never been reported.

registration.description:
Display identifier: an N-number when one is resolvable from the
aircraft's callsign or registry entry, else the uppercase ICAO
hex. Was `tail`; /v1/operations already calls this same concept
`registration`.

report_count.description: Lifetime public report count for this aircraft.

worst_axis.description: Name of the VNAP axis with the aircraft's highest violation score.

worst_axis_score.description: 0..100. Null exactly when worst_axis is null.

Operation.description: One detected operation. Field set is frozen; new database columns do not appear here.

deviation_mean_nm.description: Mean lateral deviation from the published pattern.

fraction_off_pattern.description:
Time-weighted fraction of the lap spent farther than
`constants.pattern_corridor_nm` from the selected published pattern.
A fraction in 0..1 — 0.42 means 42%. Null when no pattern was matched.

id.description: Stable identifier, also half of the cursor.

time_off_pattern_s.description: Seconds spent outside the corridor. Numerator of `fraction_off_pattern`.

time_total_s.description: Seconds of lap track measured. Denominator of `fraction_off_pattern`.

OperationsTrends.description: Field set is frozen; new database columns do not appear here.

data_since_ts.description: Unix seconds of this airport's earliest classified operation, or null if it has none yet.

monthly.description: One entry per local calendar month with at least one classified operation, oldest first.

by_emitter.description: Operation count per ICAO emitter-category bucket (A1, A2, A6, B1, B4); anything else collapses into "Other".

by_type.description: Operation count per airframe model; models outside the top 8 for the window collapse into "Other".

fraction_touch_and_go.description:
Fraction of the month's total that were touch-and-gos.
0.0, not null, in a month with zero operations.

recent_days.description: Last 10 local days with at least one classified operation, oldest first.

fraction_light_aircraft.description:
Fraction of the day's operations flown by an ICAO emitter
category A1 (light) aircraft. 0.0, not null, on a day with
zero operations.

fraction_touch_and_go.description:
Fraction of the day's operations that were touch-and-gos.
0.0, not null, on a day with zero operations.

time_of_day.description: All 24 local hours, always fully populated (zero-filled), covering the whole window.

timezone.description: IANA tz name used to bucket local days, months, and hours.

Runway.description:
No `icao` here: it duplicates the envelope's `airport_icao` and is
internal-only. All four geometry fields are non-null — the underlying
`runways` table declares them NOT NULL and every row is fully seeded.

fraction_stopped.description:
Fraction of `total` that stopped (landed at least once). Was
`stopped_pct`, a real percent (28.9) that shared a "pct" prefix
with /operations' fraction_off_pattern despite holding a
different scale. Null when `total` is 0 (no aircraft in the
window) rather than a divide-by-zero artifact.

TrackSample.description: One raw position sample. Field set is frozen.

altitude_datum.description:
The datum `altitude_ft` is measured against. Varies by `source`;
`unknown` when no altitude is present or the source does not say.

source.description: Which upstream feed supplied the sample.

is_fallback.description: True when the requested airport had no scored aircraft and a neighbour was substituted.

resolved_airport_icao.description:
The airport the offenders actually come from. Differs from
requested_airport_icao when is_fallback is true.

resolved_airport_label.description: Human-readable label (city or name) for resolved_airport_icao.

apiKeyHeader.description: Alternative to the bearer header. Identical semantics.
apiKeyHeader.name: X-API-Key

info.description:
A read-only HTTP API over four data families collected around general-aviation
airports: **classified operations** (touch-and-gos, circles, low approaches,
landings, passes), **raw ADS-B position samples**, **precomputed aggregates**
(stats, worst offenders, trends, VNAP compliance, runways, patterns, flow), and
the **KLMO fees ledger**.

Every endpoint is read-only. Nothing here mutates state.

## Authentication

Every request needs an API key, issued by an administrator. Present it either way:

```
Authorization: Bearer cj_live_0123456789abcdef_<secret>
X-API-Key: cj_live_0123456789abcdef_<secret>
```

Keys look like `cj_<env>_<id16>_<secret43>`. The `env` segment is `live` in
production. Only the id half is stored in recoverable form — the secret is
hashed, so a lost key cannot be recovered and must be reissued.

Call `GET /v1/meta` to see exactly what your own key can do. It reports your
scopes, your airport restriction, and the current limits, which makes a 403
diagnosable without contacting us.

## Scopes

A key carries any combination of four scopes. Requesting an endpoint outside
your scopes returns `403 forbidden_scope`.

| Scope | Grants |
|---|---|
| `ops:read` | `/v1/operations` |
| `tracks:read` | `/v1/tracks` |
| `aggregates:read` | the seven `/v1/airports/{icao}/…` endpoints |
| `ledger:read` | `/v1/ledger/…` |

## Airport restriction

A key may additionally be restricted to specific airports. `GET /v1/meta`
reports `"airports": null` for an unrestricted key, or a list of ICAO codes.
Requesting data for an airport outside that list returns `403
forbidden_airport` — and it returns the same 403 whether or not the airport
exists, so the restriction cannot be used to enumerate our database.

**Restricted keys must scope `/v1/tracks` by airport.** Raw track samples are
keyed by aircraft, not by airport, so an `icao24`-only query has no airport to
check. If your key is restricted, pass `airport=` (optionally alongside
`icao24=` to follow one aircraft within that airport); an `icao24`-only request
returns `403 forbidden_airport`. Unrestricted keys may query by `icao24` alone.

Note that airport scoping on tracks is **geographic**: samples are selected by a
bounding box around the field, so aircraft operating at a neighbouring airport
within that radius may appear. This is inherent to a positional query.

## Pagination

`/v1/operations` and `/v1/tracks` are keyset-paginated and return:

```json
{ "data": [ … ], "next_cursor": "MTc4NDY2NDExNjpvcC0wMDE" }
```

Pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor` to get the following page. Keep every other
parameter identical between pages. When `next_cursor` is `null` you have reached
the end. A cursor is opaque — do not parse or construct one.

A cursor is returned whenever a page came back full, so the last page of an
exact multiple of `limit` will hand you a cursor that yields an empty page. That
is normal; stop when `data` is empty or `next_cursor` is `null`.

`limit` defaults to 500 and is capped at 5000.

## Time parameters

`since` and `until` accept either a Unix timestamp in seconds (`1784664115`) or
an ISO 8601 datetime (`2026-07-21T15:00:00Z`). A datetime without a timezone is
read as UTC. Timestamps are always **returned** as Unix seconds.

`/v1/operations` defaults to the last 7 days if you omit both.
`/v1/tracks` requires both, and rejects a span longer than 31 days — page
through a longer range with the cursor.

## Rate limits

120 requests per minute per key, as a fixed window. Every response carries
`X-RateLimit-Limit` and `X-RateLimit-Remaining`; exceeding the limit returns
`429 rate_limited` with `Retry-After: 60`.

## Errors

Every error in this namespace uses one envelope:

```json
{ "error": { "code": "forbidden_scope", "message": "key lacks scope tracks:read" } }
```

Branch on `code`, not on `message` — messages may be reworded.

| Code | Status | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `unauthorized` | 401 | Missing, malformed, unknown, or revoked key |
| `invalid_request` | 400 | Bad parameter, bad cursor, or a span over the cap |
| `forbidden_scope` | 403 | Valid key without the required scope |
| `forbidden_airport` | 403 | Valid key restricted away from this airport |
| `not_found` | 404 | Unknown airport or resource |
| `rate_limited` | 429 | Over 120 requests per minute |
| `upstream_unavailable` | 503 | The ledger sidecar is unreachable or erroring |

The runway currently in use and the last twenty runway changes. `active` is
null when no flow has been established. Requires `aggregates:read`.

pattern editor. Requires `aggregates:read`.
Threshold coordinates, magnetic heading, and length per runway. Requires `aggregates:read`.

stop classification for one airport and window. Requires

get.description:
Voluntary Noise Abatement Procedure compliance scored per aircraft over the
window. Requires `aggregates:read`.

Aircraft ranked by circling behaviour and report volume. Requires
`aggregates:read`.

When the requested airport has no scored aircraft, the underlying view falls
back to the nearest neighbouring airport and sets `is_fallback: true` with
`resolved_airport_icao` naming the substitute — always check those two fields
before attributing the result. **If your key is restricted, a fallback to an
airport outside your scope is suppressed**: you receive an empty list with
`is_fallback: false`, never another field's data.

get.description:
Proxied to the ledger sidecar, which computes runway-use fees from lap and
dwell analysis. Requires `ledger:read`.

`resource` is an allowlist of exactly two values:

- `ledger` — runway uses, the daily series, the operator ledger, and the
  methodology block that ships with the numbers. Accepts `days` (1–365,
  default 30).
- `aircraft-fees` — per-aircraft runway-use totals.

Any other value returns `404 not_found`. Query parameters beginning with `_`
are stripped before forwarding.

If the sidecar is unreachable you get `503 upstream_unavailable`. If it
rejects your parameters you get `400 invalid_request` — a 503 here always
means our problem, never yours.

parameters.description: Lookback in days. Applies to `ledger` only.
parameters.name: days

200.description: Ledger payload, passed through from the sidecar.

get.description:
Echoes your key's own scopes, airport restriction, and the current limits.
Requires only a valid key — no particular scope. Use it to diagnose a 403
without contacting us.

Each row is one detected operation — a touch-and-go, circle, low approach,
landing, or pass — with the runway, pattern deviation, wind at the time, and
any resolved operator or flight school.

Requires the `ops:read` scope. Keyset-paginated, ordered by
`(timestamp_ts, id)` ascending.

get.description:
Per-aircraft position samples as recorded, without smoothing or
interpolation. This is the heaviest endpoint in the API.

Requires the `tracks:read` scope. Both `since` and `until` are required, and
the span may not exceed 31 days — page through longer ranges with the
cursor. Supply at least one of `icao24` or `airport`.

**If your key is restricted to specific airports you must pass `airport`.**
An `icao24`-only request from a restricted key returns `403
forbidden_airport`. Combine `airport` and `icao24` to follow one aircraft
within one field.

Selecting by `airport` uses a bounding box around the field, so aircraft
operating at a nearby airport inside that radius can appear.

Ordered by `(timestamp_ts, icao24)` ascending; the cursor encodes that pair.
